questions.question: What is the solution to the following system of linear equations? 3x - 9y + 4z = 5 2x + 7y + z = 12 3x - z = 0
questions.questionHtml:
What is the solution to the following system of linear equations? 

3x - 9y + 4z = 5

2x + 7y + z = 12

3x - z = 0
questions.solution:
3x - z = 0 

⇒ z = 3x 

Now substitute  z in the first and second equations, 

⇒ 3x - 9y + 4(3x) = 5  

⇒ 15x - 9y = 5 .....(4)  

⇒ 2x + 7y + z = 12 

⇒ 2x + 7y + 3x = 5  

⇒ 5x + 7y = 5 ....(5)  

Now we have a system of two equations(4,5) with two variables

 ⇒ 5x − 3y= 5/3 ​ 

⇒  5x + 7y= 12

Subtract the first equation from the second equation to eliminate x

⇒ 5x + 7y−(5x - 3y) = 12 −  5/3 ​ 

⇒ 10y = 31/3 ​   

Now substitute the value of y into the first equation to solve for x

⇒ 5x − 3(31/30) ​= ​5/3   
 
⇒ x = 143/150 ​  ​

Now that we have x and y, we can find z using the equation 

⇒ z = 3x  

⇒ z = 3 (143/150) = 143/50

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick 

(x5 - 12x4 + 12x3 - 12x2 + 12x - 1)

⇒ (x5 - 11x4 - x4 + 11x3 + x3 - 11x2 - x2 + 11x + x - 1)

⇒ x4(x - 11) - x3(x - 11) + x2(x - 11) - x(x - 11) + (x - 1)

⇒ (x - 11) [x4 - x3 + x2 - x] + (x - 1)

put x = 11

⇒ (11 - 11) [x4 - x3 + x2 - x] + (11 - 1)

⇒ 0 × [x4 - x3 + x2 - x] + (11 - 1)

⇒ (11 - 1) = 10

Hence, the correct answer is 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

If x = 11, then the value of (x5 - 12x4 + 12x3 - 12x2 + 12x - 1) is:

Formula used:

Substitute x = 11 in the polynomial expression

Calculation:

⇒ 161051 - 12×14641 + 12×1331 - 12×121 + 12×11 - 1

⇒ 161051 - 175692 + 15972 - 1452 + 132 - 1

⇒ 161051 - 175692 + 15972 - 1452 + 132 - 1

⇒ -14641 + 15972 - 1452 + 132 - 1

⇒ 1331 - 1452 + 132 - 1

⇒ 10

questions.question: If cos 2 θ - sin 2 θ - 3 cos θ + 2 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of \(1 + 5 \cos \theta + \frac{\tan \theta}{2}?\)
questions.questionHtml: If cos2 θ - sin2 θ  - 3 cos θ + 2 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of \(1 + 5 \cos \theta + \frac{\tan \theta}{2}?\)
questions.solution:
Formula:

sin2 θ = 1 - cos2 θ 

Calculation:

According to the question-

 cos2 θ - sin2 θ  - 3 cos θ + 2 = 0

⇒ cos2 θ - (1 - cos2 θ) - 3 cos θ + 2 = 0

⇒ 2cos2 θ - 3 cos θ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cos2 θ - cos θ - 2cos θ + 1 = 0

⇒ cos θ × (2cos θ - 1) -1 × (2cos θ - 1) = 0

⇒ (cos θ - 1) × (2cos θ - 1) = 0

Either cos θ = 1 i.e., θ = 0º (not possible) or cos θ = \(1\over2\) i.e., θ = 60º

Substiuting the value of θ in the equation-

\(1 + 5 \cos \theta + \frac{\tan \theta}{2}\)

⇒ 1 + 5 cos 60º + \(tan 60\over 2\)

⇒ 1 + (5 × \(1\over2\)) + \(\sqrt3\over2\) = \(\frac{7+\sqrt 3}{2}\)

∴ The answer is \(\frac{7+\sqrt 3}{2}\).

questions.question: If 3 tan θ = \(2\sqrt 3 \) sin θ , 0° < θ < 90 °, then the value of \(\frac{3}{4}\left( {\frac{{{\rm{cose}}{{\rm{c}}^2}\,2{\rm{\theta }}\,{\rm{ + }}\,{\rm{co}}{{\rm{t}}^2}2{\rm{\theta }}}}{{{\rm{si}}{{\rm{n}}^2}\,{\rm{\theta }}\,{\rm{ + }}\,{\rm{ta}}{{\rm{n}}^2}2{\rm{\theta }}}}} \right)\) is:
questions.questionHtml: If 3 tan θ = \(2\sqrt 3 \) sin θ, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of \(\frac{3}{4}\left( {\frac{{{\rm{cose}}{{\rm{c}}^2}\,2{\rm{\theta }}\,{\rm{ + }}\,{\rm{co}}{{\rm{t}}^2}2{\rm{\theta }}}}{{{\rm{si}}{{\rm{n}}^2}\,{\rm{\theta }}\,{\rm{ + }}\,{\rm{ta}}{{\rm{n}}^2}2{\rm{\theta }}}}} \right)\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: 3 tan θ = 2√3 sin θ

⇒ 3 × (sin θ / cos θ) = 2√3 sin θ ⇒ cos θ = 3 / 2√3 = √3 / 2 ⇒ θ = 30°

Substitute θ = 30° in the expression: (3/4) × [ (cosec2 60° + cot2 60°) ÷ (sin2 30° + tan2 60°) ]

⇒ (3/4) × [ (4/3 + 1/3) ÷ (1/4 + 3) ]

⇒ (3/4) × [ (5/3) ÷ (13/4) ] = (3/4) × (5/3) × (4/13) = 5/13

∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Alternate Method

Given:

3 tan θ = 2√3 sin θ

Formula Used:

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ

cosec θ = 1 / sin θ , cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

Calculations:

⇒ 3 × (sin θ / cos θ) = 2√3 sin θ

Since 0° < θ < 90°, sin θ ≠ 0. Dividing both sides by sin θ:

⇒ 3 / cos θ = 2√3

⇒ cos θ = 3 / (2√3)

⇒ cos θ = √3 / 2

⇒ θ = 30°

We need to find the value of:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (cosec2 2θ + cot2 2θ) / (sin2 θ + tan2 2θ) ]

Substituting θ = 30° into the expression:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (cosec2 60° + cot2 60°) / (sin2 30° + tan2 60°) ]

Using standard trigonometric values:

⇒ cosec 60° = 2 / √3 ⇒ cosec2 60° = 4 / 3

⇒ cot 60° = 1 / √3 ⇒ cot2 60° = 1 / 3

⇒ sin 30° = 1 / 2 ⇒ sin2 30° = 1 / 4

⇒ tan 60° = √3 ⇒ tan2 60° = 3

Putting these values in the expression:

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (4/3 + 1/3) / (1/4 + 3) ]

⇒ (3 / 4) × [ (5/3) / (13/4) ]

⇒ (3 / 4) × (5 / 3) × (4 / 13)

⇒ 60 / 156

⇒ 5 / 13

∴ The correct answer is 5/13.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

The three primary Pythagorean identities are: sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ, and 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ.

Values of Trigonometric Ratios

Key values to remember for 30° and 60° angles: sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2, sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2, and tan 60° = √3.

Signs of Trigonometric Functions

In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), all six basic trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan, cosec, sec, cot) yield positive values.

questions.solution:
Given:

\(p + \frac{1}{9}\sqrt p + {k^2}\)

Formula used:

\(x^2+2xy+ {y^2}=(x+y)^2\)
Calculation:

For  \(p + \frac{1}{9}\sqrt p + {k^2}\)  to be a perfect square, \(p + \frac{1}{9}\sqrt p + {k^2}=\left( \sqrt p+\frac{1}{18}\right)^2\).

And \(\left( \sqrt p+\frac{1}{18}\right)^2= p + \frac{1}{9}\sqrt p + \frac{1}{18^2}\)

Therefore,  \(k = \pm \frac{1}{18}\).

∴ The values of k for which the expression \(p + \frac{1}{9}\sqrt p + {k^2}\)  is a perfect square are \(\pm \frac{1}{18}\).

questions.question: For which of the following values of a and b do the given equations, have NO solution? x - ay = 2 - a (1 - a)x + 6y = a + b
questions.questionHtml:
For which of the following values of a and b do the given equations, have NO solution?
x - ay = 2 - a
(1 - a)x + 6y = a + b
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For linear equations to have no solution, the condition is: a1 / a2 = b1 / b2 ≠ c1 / c2.

Equating coefficients of x and y: 1 ÷ (1 − a) = −a ÷ 6 ⇒ a2 − a − 6 = 0 ⇒ a = 3 or −2.

Based on the given options, taking a = 3, the ratio becomes −3 ÷ 6 = −1/2.

Applying the inequality to constant terms: (2 − a) ÷ (a + b) ≠ −1/2.

Substituting a = 3 gives: −1 ÷ (3 + b) ≠ −1/2 ⇒ 3 + b ≠ 2 ⇒ b ≠ −1.

∴ The correct answer is a = 3, b ≠ -1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Equation 1: x − ay = 2 − a

Equation 2: (1 − a)x + 6y = a + b

Formula Used:

For a system of linear equations a1x + b1y = c1 and a2x + b2y = c2 to have no solution:

⇒ a1 / a2 = b1 / b2 ≠ c1 / c2

Calculations:

Comparing the given equations with standard form:

⇒ a1 = 1, b1 = −a, c1 = 2 − a

⇒ a2 = (1 − a), b2 = 6, c2 = a + b

Equating the ratios for no solution:

⇒ 1 / (1 − a) = −a / 6 ≠ (2 − a) / (a + b)

Solving the first part (equality):

⇒ 1 / (1 − a) = −a / 6

⇒ 6 = −a(1 − a)

⇒ 6 = −a + a2

⇒ a2 − a − 6 = 0

⇒ a2 − 3a + 2a − 6 = 0

⇒ a(a − 3) + 2(a − 3) = 0

⇒ (a − 3)(a + 2) = 0

⇒ a = 3 or a = −2

Since a = 3 is provided in the options, we proceed with a = 3.

Substituting a = 3 in the second part (inequality):

⇒ −a / 6 ≠ (2 − a) / (a + b)

⇒ −3 / 6 ≠ (2 − 3) / (3 + b)

⇒ −1 / 2 ≠ −1 / (3 + b)

⇒ 1 / 2 ≠ 1 / (3 + b)

Cross multiplying gives:

⇒ 3 + b ≠ 2

⇒ b ≠ 2 − 3

⇒ b ≠ −1

∴ The correct answer is a = 3, b ≠ -1.

Additional Information

Unique Solution

The system of equations has exactly one solution (lines intersect at exactly one point). Condition: a1 / a2 ≠ b1 / b2.

No Solution

The system of equations has no solution (lines are strictly parallel and never intersect). Condition: a1 / a2 = b1 / b2 ≠ c1 / c2.

Infinitely Many Solutions

The system of equations has infinitely many solutions (lines are coincident or overlap completely). Condition: a1 / a2 = b1 / b2 = c1 / c2.

questions.question: If \(\frac{1}{{1\, + \,\tan \,{\rm{\theta }}}}\, + \,\frac{1}{{1\, - \,\tan \,{\rm{\theta }}}}\, = \,4\) , 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of cosec θ + sec θ + sin θ?
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{1}{{1\, + \,\tan \,{\rm{\theta }}}}\, + \,\frac{1}{{1\, - \,\tan \,{\rm{\theta }}}}\, = \,4\), 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of cosec θ + sec θ + sin θ?
questions.solution:
Formula:

tan θ = \(sinθ \over cosθ \)

cos2 θ = 1 - sin2 θ  

Calculation:

\(\frac{1}{{1\, + \,\tan \,{\rm{θ }}}}\, + \,\frac{1}{{1\, - \,\tan \,{\rm{θ }}}}\, = \,4\)

⇒ \(1\over 1+ {sinθ \over cos θ }\) + \(1\over 1- {sinθ \over cos θ }\) = 4

⇒  \(cosθ\over cosθ+ {sinθ }\) + \(cosθ\over cosθ - {sinθ }\) = 4

⇒ \(cos^2θ-cosθ \times sinθ + cos^2θ + sinθ cosθ \over cos^2θ- {sin^2θ }\) = 4

⇒ \(2cos^2θ \over cos^2θ- {sin^2θ }\) = 4

⇒ \(2cos^2θ \over cos^2θ- ({1-cos^2θ })\)= 4

⇒ \(2cos^2θ \over 2cos^2θ- 1\)= 4

⇒ 2cos2 θ = 8cos2 θ - 4

⇒ 6cos2 θ = 4 or cos2 θ = \(2\over3\)

We know that cos2 θ = 1 - sin2 θ  

⇒ \(2\over3\) = 1 - sin2 θ  

⇒ sin2 θ = 1 - \(2\over3\) = \(1\over3\)

⇒ sin θ = \(1\over\sqrt3\)

⇒ cosec θ = √3

Substiuting the values, we get-

cosec θ + sec θ + sin θ

⇒ √3 + \(\sqrt3\over\sqrt2\) + \(1\over\sqrt3\)

⇒ \(3\sqrt2 +3 +\sqrt2\over\sqrt6\)

⇒ \(\frac{{3\, + \,4\sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 6 }}\)

∴ The value of the expression is \(\frac{{3\, + \,4\sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 6 }}\).

questions.solution:
\(\rm \frac{2x}{x+2}+ \frac{1}{2x+4}- \frac{12-x}{2x^2+4x}=a+\frac{b}{x}\) ⇒ \(\rm \frac{2x}{x+2}+ \frac{1}{2(x+2)}- \frac{12-x}{2x(x+2)}=a+\frac{b}{x}\)

⇒ \(\rm \frac{1}{(x+2)}[2x+ \frac{1}{2}- \frac{12-x}{2x}]=a+\frac{b}{x}\) ⇒ \(\rm \frac{1}{(x+2)}[\frac{4x^2+x-12+x}{2x}]=a+\frac{b}{x}\) ⇒ \(\frac{2x^2+4x-3x-6}{x(x+2)}=a+\frac{b}{x}\) 

⇒ \(\frac{2x(x+2)-3(x+2)}{x(x+2)}=a+\frac{b}{x}\) ⇒ \(\frac{(2x-3)(x+2)}{x(x+2)}=a+\frac{b}{x}\) ⇒ \(\frac{(2x-3)}{x}=a+\frac{b}{x}\) ⇒ \( 2+\frac{(-3)}{x}=a+\frac{b}{x}\)

On comparing both sides, we get

⇒ a = 2 and b = -3 ⇒ ab = 2 × (-3) ⇒ ab = -6

questions.solution:
Given:

3x(3x - 8) + y(y + 1) + 4z2 - 2z + \(16\frac{1}{2}\) = 0

Formula used:

(a + b)2 = a2 + b2 + 2ab

Calculation:

3x(3x - 8) + y(y + 1) + 4z2 - 2z + \(16\frac{1}{2}\) = 0

⇒ 9x2 - 24x + y2 + y + 4z2 - 2z + 16\(1\over2\)= 0

⇒ 9x2 - 24x + (4)2 + y2 + y + (1/2)2 + 4z2 - 2z + (1/2)2 = 0

⇒ (3x)2 - 24x + (4)2] + [(y)2 + y + (1/2)2] + [(2z)2 - 2z + (1/2)2] = 0

⇒ (3x - 4)2 + (y + \(1\over2\))2 + (2z - \(1\over2\))2 = 0

⇒ 3x - 4 = 0; y + \(1\over2\) = 0; 2z - \(1\over2\) = 0

⇒ 3x = 4; y = -1/2; 2z = 1/2

⇒ x = 4/3; y = - 1/2; z = 1/4

6x + y + 2z = 6(4/3) + (-1/2) + 2 × (1/4)

⇒ 8 - (1/2) + (1/2)

⇒ 8

∴ The value of (6x + y + 2z) is 8.

Given:

[(3x√y + 2y√x)/(3x√y - 2y√x)] - [(3x√y - 2y√x)/(3x√y + 2y√x)] = √x × √y

Concept Used:

We need to take LCM and simplify the equation.

Formula Used:

(a + b)2 - (a - b)2 = 4ab

(a2 - b2) = (a + b)(a - b)

Calculation:

Take a = 3x√y and b = 2y√x

Given expression will be transformed to [(a + b)/(a - b)] - [(a - b)/(a + b)]

⇒ [(a + b)2 - (a - b)2]/[(a + b)(a - b)] = √(xy)

⇒ 4ab/(a2 - b2) = √(xy)

⇒ (4 ×  3x√y × 2y√x)/[(3x√y)2 - (2y√x)2] = √(xy)

⇒ (24x√x × y√y)/(9x2y - 4y2x) = √(xy)

⇒ [24 × xy × √(xy)]/[(xy)(9x - 4y) = √(xy)

⇒ 24/(9x - 4y) = 1

⇒ 9x - 4y = 24

∴ The correct relation between x and y is 9x - 4y = 24

Now,

⇒ (x3 + 1/x3) (x3 - 1/x3) = 235√2 × 49√46 = 23030\(\sqrt{23}\)
